scenes.tts: The microglia in your brain were not made by your brain. In mice, most of them descend from cells born in the yolk sac, a membrane outside the embryo, before the brain had a blood-brain barrier. Glia is a job description, not a family. So where does each kind of glial cell come from?
scenes.visual: A brain with a microglia cell and a crossed-out 'made here?'; a yolk sac appears outside and sends a cell in; then four glial cells in a row, each with a red question mark.
scenes.narration: The microglia in your brain were not made by your brain. In mice, most of them descend from cells born in the yolk sac, a membrane outside the embryo, before the brain had a blood-brain barrier. Glia is a job description, not a family. So where does each kind of glial cell come from?

scenes.tts: Lineage methods gave the answer. Astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and ependymal cells come from the neuroepithelium of the neural tube, mostly through the radial glia that also made the neurons. Microglia come from the yolk sac. Schwann cells and satellite glia come from the neural crest, the cells that leave the edges of the closing neural tube. Three birthplaces, one name.
scenes.visual: The four cells fly to three sources: a neural tube with radial glia, a yolk sac, and a neural crest streaming from a tube.
scenes.narration: Lineage methods gave the answer. scenes.tts: Begin in the neural tube. In the mouse cortex, radial glia make neurons first, and most astrocytes appear late. The same progenitors change their output. In cultured rodent cortical progenitors, the cytokine C N T F drives cells to make G F A P, the standard astrocyte marker. It acts through J A K and S T A T three. Early on, the S T A T three site in the G F A P promoter is methylated, so the cell cannot read it. Later the site is demethylated. One proposal is that newborn neurons make a different cytokine, cardiotrophin one.
scenes.caption: Begin in the neural tube. In the mouse cortex, radial glia make neurons first, and most astrocytes appear late. The same progenitors change their output. In cultured rodent cortical progenitors, the cytokine CNTF drives cells to make GFAP, the standard astrocyte marker. It acts through JAK and STAT3. Early on, the STAT3 site in the GFAP promoter is methylated, so the cell cannot read it. Later the site is demethylated. One proposal is that newborn neurons make a different cytokine, cardiotrophin-1.
scenes.visual: A radial glial cell releases white neurons, then green astrocytes; it grows into a wide cell where CNTF acts through JAK and STAT3; the STAT3 site on the GFAP gene is methylated (GFAP off) then demethylated; newborn neurons send a separately coloured, proposed cytokine, cardiotrophin-1.

scenes.tts: Oligodendrocytes start in a ventral strip. In the spinal cord, Sonic hedgehog from the floor plate divides the ventral cord into progenitor domains. One of them, p M N, expresses Olig two. In mice and chicks, p M N first makes motor neurons, then oligodendrocyte precursors. Mice lacking both Olig one and Olig two have no spinal motor neurons and no spinal oligodendrocytes.
scenes.caption: Oligodendrocytes start in a ventral strip. In the spinal cord, Sonic hedgehog from the floor plate divides the ventral cord into progenitor domains. One of them, pMN, expresses Olig2. In mice and chicks, pMN first makes motor neurons, then oligodendrocyte precursors. Mice lacking both Olig1 and Olig2 have no spinal motor neurons and no spinal oligodendrocytes.
scenes.visual: A stack of progenitor domains over a floor plate with a hedgehog arrow; the pMN band lights up and emits motor neurons, then oligodendrocyte precursors; with Olig1 and Olig2 removed the band greys and both outputs are crossed out.

scenes.tts: Microglia are the odd ones out. To trace them, researchers gave mice one dose of tamoxifen at about embryonic day seven point five. That permanently marked yolk-sac cells and all their descendants. In adults, about a third of microglia carried the mark. Very few blood cells did. Embryos without a heartbeat made yolk-sac macrophages but no brain microglia. So the progenitors travel in through the early circulation.

scenes.tts: In the peripheral nervous system, glia come from the neural crest. Schwann cells pass through steps: crest cell, then Schwann cell precursor, then immature Schwann cell. In culture, the precursors die unless neurons are present. Neuregulin, a growth factor on axons, can keep them alive. Mice without the receptor E r b B three lack precursors along their nerves. So ask where a glial cell was born, and which signal it needs.
